items.title: CVE-2026-89049: SSRF in AWS Systems Manager Agent remote-host port forwarding
items.summary: AWS says SSM Agent versions earlier than 3.3.4851.0 are affected by an SSRF in Session Manager remote-host port forwarding that can reach link-local endpoints.
items.whyItMatters: A principal allowed to start remote-host port-forwarding sessions could reach instance metadata and use the managed instance's temporary IAM role credentials outside the instance.
checks: Inventory SSM Agent versions and prioritize upgrades to version 3.3.4851.0 or later.
Review who can call ssm:StartSession with AWS-StartPortForwardingSessionToRemoteHost, including access to that SSM document.
Review CloudTrail StartSession activity for that document and investigate sessions that do not match an approved support path.

mapping.basis: The affected component is SSM Agent and the vulnerable feature is Session Manager remote-host port forwarding.

mapping.term: managed EC2 instances and Instance Metadata Service
mapping.basis: The bulletin describes managed EC2 instances and access to the instance metadata service through the affected tunnel.
The stated impact includes theft and off-instance use of temporary instance-role credentials.

items.basis: TRACE-reviewed AWS Security Bulletin 2026-107-AWS, corroborated by the AWS-maintained amazon-ssm-agent GitHub security advisory.

items.title: Updated GuardDuty service-linked role (SLR)
items.summary: AWS added vpc-lattice:CreateServiceNetworkVpcAssociation and vpc-lattice:AssociateViaAWSService to the GuardDuty service-linked role for Runtime Monitoring agent connectivity.
items.whyItMatters: The GuardDuty-owned role now has two additional network-association capabilities. Their expected service use should be distinguished from unexpected principal-created VPC Lattice associations.
checks: Review the current AmazonGuardDutyServiceRolePolicy version and the two added VPC Lattice actions.
Baseline VPC Lattice association activity attributable to AWSServiceRoleForAmazonGuardDuty before alerting on similar principal activity.
Confirm Runtime Monitoring connectivity and its network controls in each enabled account and Region.

mapping.basis: The update changes the AWS-managed service-linked role used by GuardDuty.
The added actions create and associate VPC Lattice service-network connectivity for Runtime Monitoring.

items.basis: TRACE-reviewed entry in the official Amazon GuardDuty documentation history and the linked service-role permissions page.

items.title: Updated Network Scanning informational findings details
items.summary: AWS clarified that Network Scanning creates an Informational finding when no supported open ports are detected, and described how that finding changes across later scans.
items.whyItMatters: An Informational result confirms that an eligible resource was scanned; the absence of any finding does not establish that Network Scanning examined the resource.
checks: Confirm Network Scanning is enabled in the intended accounts and Regions before interpreting its findings.
Treat an Informational no-open-ports finding as evidence of a completed scan, not as a permanent reachability guarantee.
Reconcile missing findings with supported resource types, scan timing, exclusions, and the documented finding lifecycle.

mapping.term: Security Hub Network Scanning informational findings
mapping.basis: The update changes how Security Hub Network Scanning informational findings should be interpreted.

items.basis: TRACE-reviewed official Security Hub documentation-history entry and the current Network Scanning finding-lifecycle documentation.

items.title: New feature - Custom Detection Rules
items.summary: GuardDuty now provides AWS-maintained rules for selected threat techniques, with per-account live or 14-day dry-run associations and organization-level configuration.
items.whyItMatters: Teams can evaluate account-specific unwanted CloudTrail activity in dry-run mode before enabling findings, then manage associations consistently from a delegated GuardDuty administrator.
checks: Inventory available rules and select only techniques that should be exceptional in the target accounts.
Use dry-run associations first and review the emitted CloudWatch match metrics during the documented 14-day window.
Confirm organization targeting, delegated-administrator ownership, and live-mode finding routing before broad rollout.

mapping.basis: Custom Detection Rules are configured and evaluated by GuardDuty.
AWS documents that the rules evaluate selected fields in CloudTrail management events.
AWS documents CloudWatch match metrics as the output of dry-run associations.

items.basis: TRACE-reviewed official GuardDuty documentation for Custom Detection Rules; operational claims are limited to the documented rule, association, mode, and signal model.

items.title: Password-spraying campaign targeted AWS root users at more than 150 organizations
items.summary: Datadog Security Research observed repeated failed AWS root-user console sign-ins from July 24 through August 23, 2026; it reported no successful authentication in the observed activity.
items.whyItMatters: The activity supplies a concrete CloudTrail hunt while reinforcing separate controls for member-account root credentials and the AWS Organizations management account.
checks: Search CloudTrail for Root ConsoleLogin failures and successes, then compare the user agents and time window documented in the research.
Review whether root credentials have been removed from eligible Organizations member accounts through centralized root access.
Alert on direct root sign-ins, root API activity, credential changes, and privileged sts:AssumeRoot sessions.

mapping.basis: The campaign targeted AWS account root identities and the official countermeasures are documented by IAM.
The research and AWS guidance distinguish centralized member-account root controls from management-account safeguards.
The observed signal is failed or successful root ConsoleLogin activity recorded in CloudTrail.

items.basis: TRACE-reviewed independent research. Observed scope and outcome are attributed to Datadog; defensive interpretation is corroborated with AWS root-user guidance.
